summary: Block on prior art and novelty scope. The Petit-Kosters-Messeng source already supplies the multiplicative-subgroup composed map, fixed-Q relation sampling through R = aP + bQ, direct System (4), heuristic relation yield, and the partial cost expression while leaving the decisive generalized-root term open. The Amadori-Pintore-Sala source independently overlaps the one-system summation-polynomial relation strategy and likewise leaves its solver-term comparison unproved without a sub-square-root conclusion. TASK-027 adds an exact factor-base census and finite orbit counts; TASK-028 adds exact source specialization and a derived target-bound sound acceptance filter. Neither contribution changes the algorithmic mechanism, proves complete recovery, nor supplies a new cost-changing solver bound. The proposal and design also state that the mechanism identity is unchanged from HGP-M16-SOLVER-SLOPE-001 and that it is new to neither the repository nor the reviewed corpus. Its proposed sparse-elimination premise is therefore a duplicate or semantic re-encoding rather than a novel mechanism. The proposal truthfully disclaims global novelty, but it cannot satisfy the required repository/corpus novelty scope, so the policy blocker novelty_scope_overclaimed applies. Primary-source full-text extracts and precise locators are present; no missing-primary-source blocker is assigned.
